outcome: consistency of urodynamic observations with pre-urodynamic diagnosis
impact on patient management (cancellation or modification of planned surgery)
cohort: 2,053 female patients who underwent urodynamic evaluation prior to surgery for stress urinary incontinence in six referral Italian centers between 2008 and 2013.
finding: Urodynamic observations were inconsistent with pre-urodynamic diagnoses in 62.2% of patients, leading to cancellation or modification of planned surgery in 19.2% of cases, particularly highlighting that 'uncomplicated' patients are a minority and UDS seems mandatory for 'complicated' cases.
